title: Carry runtime timezone data when executing cross-built Go tests
applies_when: An exact Go test executable is cross-built for Windows or a stripped runtime without a local Go installation or IANA timezone database, and tests fail in time.LoadLocation despite passing on the build host.
lesson: A Go executable and its source hashes do not account for all runtime data. Check the LoadLocation lookup order: process ZONEINFO, Unix system database, GOROOT/lib/time/zoneinfo.zip, then an imported time/tzdata package. Preserve the failed run and reuse the identical executable in a fresh process with a task-private, hash-verified zoneinfo.zip from the reviewed Go distribution. In mapstructure at 52aa5c6d, only named-location cases failed in a Windows environment without that data; supplying ZONEINFO resolved them without changing source, tests or the binary. Keep the selected archive/version and child environment in reproduction records. Do not patch a decoder or weaken assertions merely to compensate for missing runtime data.
avoid_when: This does not establish that every timezone failure is environmental. A wrong location name, malformed archive, historical offset expectation, embedded tzdata or actual decoder regression requires its own check. UTC and Local succeeding do not prove named-location data exists. Do not alter system timezone settings or another task's environment. A successful Linux build is not Windows execution, and Windows non-race tests are not a race/version-matrix qualification. Reading this advice alone establishes no measured setup savings or Scout-yield improvement.

evidence.note: Official documentation specifies the timezone database lookup order and the ZONEINFO directory or uncompressed ZIP option. This supports the runtime-data mechanism, not any unpublished full-suite count.
The tested Go distribution's implementation loads timezone data at runtime. Recheck the target version rather than assuming an installed build host's data is embedded in every executable.
StringToTimeLocationHookFunc reaches time.LoadLocation. The supported public hook can therefore expose a missing-runtime-data failure without a source defect.
